script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

---

FADE IN:

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

JAMES (30s, wearing glasses, disheveled, clutching a mug of coffee) sits at a table, staring at his phone. Across the room, THOMAS (30s, well-dressed, carrying a briefcase) enters, sees James, and makes his way over.

THOMAS
(cheerfully)
Hey, James. I didn't see you at the office yesterday.

JAMES
(grudgingly)
I took a sick day.

Thomas sits down across from James.

THOMAS
You sure you're okay? You've seemed off lately.

James looks up, avoiding Thomas's gaze.

JAMES
I've just got a lot on my mind.

Thomas reaches across the table and places a hand on James's shoulder.

THOMAS
Well, if there's anything I can do to help, you know I'm here for you.

James hesitates, then finally meets Thomas's eyes.

JAMES
I appreciate that, Thomas. But there's nothing you can do.

Thomas smiles sadly and nods.

CUT TO:

INT. JAMES'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

James sits on his couch, staring at a photo of him and Thomas from college. He looks lost in thought. There's a knock at the door. It's SARAH (late 20s, cheerful, wearing a backpack).

SARAH
(excitedly)
James! I have the best news! I got the job at the marketing firm!

James stands up and hugs Sarah.

JAMES
That's amazing, Sarah. I'm so proud of you.

Sarah pulls back and notices James's somber expression.

SARAH
What's wrong, James? You don't seem yourself lately.

James sighs and sits back down on the couch.

JAMES
It's just... life, I guess. Work, bills, responsibilities. It all feels so heavy sometimes.

Sarah sits down next to him and puts a comforting hand on his shoulder.

SARAH
But you have friends, James. People who care about you. Thomas, for example.

James looks up at Sarah, surprised.

JAMES
You think Thomas cares about me?

SARAH
Of course he does. You two have been friends since college. And he's always been there for you.

James nods thoughtfully.

CUT TO:

EXT. PARK - DAY

James and Thomas sit on a bench, surrounded by cherry blossoms. They chat amicably about their jobs, their families, and their plans for the future.

THOMAS
You know, James, I've noticed you've been off lately. Is there something you want to talk about?

James looks at Thomas, considering.

JAMES
I've just been feeling... lost, I guess. Like I'm not making a difference in the world.

Thomas puts a hand on James's shoulder.

THOMAS
But you are, James. You have a good heart, and you make a difference in people's lives every day, even if it doesn't always feel that way.

James smiles, touched by Thomas's words.

CUT TO:

INT. JAMES'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

James sits at his desk, staring at his computer screen. He's been job hunting for weeks, but nothing seems to be panning out. Suddenly, there's a knock at the door. It's Thomas.

THOMAS
Hey, James. I heard about the job rejections. I'm here if you want to talk about it.

James looks up, surprised.

JAMES
How did you know?

Thomas smiles.

THOMAS
I've been keeping an eye on you, James. I care about you, and I want to help in any way I can.

James stands up and walks over to Thomas, who is sitting at the kitchen table. They talk for hours, sharing stories and laughing together.

CUT TO:

EXT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

James and Thomas sit outside the coffee shop, watching the world go by. They talk about their plans for the future and make a pact to always be there for each other, no matter what.

FADE OUT.

---

THE END
